text: Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture from north London as Tottenham host Wolves!
Tottenham are looking good for a return to the Champions League following a strong start to 2024.

Indeed, Ange Postecoglou's men are unbeaten in their last five Premier League games, winning each of their last five at home, and last week's dramatic victory over Brighton and Hove Albion felt like an important moment in the battle for a top-four finish.
With Aston Villa losing to Manchester United, Spurs moved one point clear of their rivals in fourth, and they will be looking to maintain their positive momentum here.
Also on the menu is a dose of revenge, over a side who inflicted one of Spurs' most gut-wrenching defeats under Postecoglou...
Indeed, Wolves trailed in November's reverse fixture until the 90:03 mark, when Pablo Sarabia's incredible touch and finish dragged them level before Mario Lemina hit a 97th-minute winner.
That is one of several memorable successes Gary O'Neil has masterminded over the Premier League's elite this season, with Wolves also winning 4-2 at Chelsea on their last road trip.
However, they fell to a demoralising 2-0 defeat to Brentford last week, losing star forward Matheus Cunha to injury in the process – how will they handle his absence here?
Tottenham make four changes to the side which beat Brighton in dramatic circumstances last week.
The headline news is that Son makes his first start since returning from the Asian Cup, having come off the bench to assist Johnson's winner last time out.
Bissouma, Emerson and Davies are also brought in, with Werner and Bentancur dropping to the bench and Destiny Udogie and Pedro Porro out injured.
O'Neil, meanwhile, makes just one alteration to the Wolves team beaten by Brentford last Saturday.
Cunha is sidelined with a hamstring injury, and it's Hwang – making his first appearance since the Asian Cup – who sees off competition from Bellegarde to start in his place.
Elsewhere, Mario Lemina's younger brother Noha travelled with the squad for this game, but he misses out on a place on the bench.
Since their return to the Premier League in 2018, Wolves have posted three away wins over Tottenham, with only Chelsea and Liverpool (four each) recording more in that span.
Can they cause Spurs more problems here? We're about to find out – kick-off is rapidly approaching!
We're under way at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, with Spurs kitted out in all white and Wolves in their red and green change kit.
Spurs are immediately on the front foot as Kulusevski and Maddison work the ball out left to Son.
The play eventually comes all the way back across to Richarlison, whose teasing delivery is headed behind by Kilman.
Tottenham fail to make anything of their early corner as Toti heads clear for Wolves.
Spurs only needed three minutes to go ahead in the reverse fixture and led for 87 minutes, only to collapse spectacularly in stoppage time.
Davies looks for Maddison's run with a clever ball inside from the left touchline, and Sa has to race to the edge of his box to clear.
Spurs come straight back and Maddison dummies a cutback for Richarlison, but he's crowded out and Wolves eventually survive.
Dawson stays down holding his head after Sa catches Son's cross at his near post.
The Wolves man is eventually back to his feet, though, and he will be fine to carry on.
Save! Wolves get their first chance to break as Hwang helps the ball right to Sarabia.
The Spaniard cuts inside to shoot from 25 yards out, but it's comfortably claimed by Vicario.
MASSIVE CHANCE FOR WOLVES! How is it not 1-0?! Wolves press high and Lemina recovers possession in a good area, with Sarabia eventually finding Semedo in space on the right side of the box.
His powerful strike is pushed out by Vicario, then Hwang somehow blazes over on the follow-up from six yards out.
The flag stayed down, and he should have scored!
Hwang already has 10 Premier League goals this season, two more than he managed in his two previous campaigns combined (five in 2021-22, three in 2022-23).
He should have got his 11th there.
Wolves have succeeded in slowing the pace of the game since Dawson's head injury, which came after a blistering start from Tottenham.
They get another chance to break as Sarabia releases Semedo on the overlap, but his cross is far too heavy for Neto at the back post.
There were questions as to how Wolves would line up in Cunha's absence, and Neto has started this game out on the left.
Sarabia is drifting infield from the other side, with Hwang leading the line.
Sarabia looks for Neto with an ambitious ball in behind, but Vicario gets out to claim it.
Tottenham have found it tough against Wolves lately, losing three of their last four Premier League games against them, including their dramatic defeat in the reverse fixture.
The visitors are enjoying a positive spell here.
OVER! Spurs work it patiently from left to right, and Kulusevski's dinked cross is headed out by Semedo.
It only reaches Davies on the edge of the box, and the stand-in left-back sends a powerful volley spiralling over Sa's crossbar.
Unlucky!
Save! It's another dangerous break from Wolves! Neto gets his head up on the left and finds Sarabia on the edge of the box with an outswinging cross.
The Spaniard just fails to find space for a shot so tees up Ait-Nouri, who cuts onto his right foot before bending an effort towards the bottom-right corner.
It lacks the power to beat Vicario, though, and he drops to his left to hold it.
There's a concern for Wolves here, with Lemina down after an aerial duel with Richarlison, who nudged him in the back.
The midfielder receives treatment near the edge of his own box as O'Neil takes the chance to pass on some tactical instructions.
Lemina is still laid out on his back, receiving attention from the medical staff.
It looks like it could be a head or neck injury, so all the necessary checks must take place.
Lemina is back on his feet now, which is a positive sight for Wolves.
He has been absolutely crucial in the heart of O'Neil's two-man midfield this season.
Wolves play on with 10 men as the play resumes, with Lemina forced to spend a few moments on the sidelines before being beckoned back onto the pitch by referee Anthony Taylor.
He looks fine to continue.

Close! What a cross that is from Son! He whips a teasing, left-footed delivery right across the face of goal, but neither Richarlison nor Kulusevski is attacking it and Toti can make the late decision to let it run.
It only needed a touch!
Wolves break again and Ait-Nouri fires a pass up the sideline for Hwang to chase.
Neto is with the South Korean, but Van de Ven uses his recovery pace to snuff out the danger.
Wolves win the ball back and come again, but Neto can't direct his header towards goal from Sarabia's cross.
Tottenham have scored in 36 successive Premier League matches.

Only Arsenal, who netted in 55 straight between May 2001 and November 2002, have ever enjoyed a longer run in the competition, though the last team to shut Spurs out in the top flight was Wolves last March, winning 1-0 under Julen Lopetegui at Molineux.
They're moving the ball patiently now, with Wolves sitting back in their 3-4-3 shape.

Wolves are getting so much space on the counterattack, but they're not making the most of it! Gomes surges through midfield and has both Neto and Hwang breaking ahead of him, but his pass towards the former is too powerful and runs out of play.
Sarr gets up on the underlap to receive Kulusevski's pass, and Toti steps in to trip him right before he can reach the penalty area.
Maddison is stood over this free-kick, which will come from a crossing position on the right.
Maddison's cross is only half cleared as Tottenham pack the box, and Richarlison nearly gets onto the second delivery into the area, with Dawson edging him out to put it behind for a corner.
Danger! Maddison's corner is headed away by the towering Dawson, but it goes straight back to Maddison and he wins another set-piece off Kilman.
Sa goes down as the next corner is delivered onto the edge of the six-yard box, but Wolves eventually scramble it clear.
This is much better from Spurs after a difficult period.
Ait-Nouri shows great feet on the left-hand side, tricking his way past Emerson before looking to release Neto.
That man Van de Ven is there to mop up the danger, though, speeding back to make the interception.
Another opening for Wolves! Hwang speeds onto a pass into the left-hand channel before brilliantly sitting Van de Ven down as he cuts back onto his right foot.
He then finds Gomes near the penalty spot, but he takes too long to release his pass to the unmarked Semedo and the chance is gone!
We're past the half-hour mark here, and we've been treated to an open, watchable game so far.
Wolves have had to absorb plenty of pressure but as always, Spurs have given up lots of space on the counterattack.
Wolves have just failed to punish them so far.
The home fans sound their frustrations again as the ball is worked wide to Sarr, who lets it slip under his boot and out of play.
Tottenham need more composure in front of a packed Wolves defence.
Both teams have attempted four shots so far, but Spurs are yet to hit the target with any of theirs, while Wolves have done so three times.
The visitors are also edging the expected goals (xG) battle, 0.42-0.29.
There are more audible groans from the home fans as Sarabia, then Ait-Nouri, win fouls in midfield.
Wolves have done well to frustrate the crowd so far.
Wide! That's more like it from Spurs.
Van de Ven steps out of defence before finding Maddison in space on the edge of the box.
He cuts the ball back for Kulusevski, but under close pressure, he can only awkwardly stab wide of the near post.

Anthony Taylor has a wry smile on his face here, what a defensive header that is! Van de Ven steps forward to help the ball back towards the Wolves box, but it strikes the referee on the head and rebounds to Neto! Spurs get the ball back, but Emerson's cross is held by Sa.
We're into the final five minutes of the first 45, and Spurs are just struggling to get going.
Emerson moves into a midfield position but then sprays a terrible ball out of play on the opposite side, gifting Wolves possession back.
Now Wolves push their hosts back, with Neto dropping a shoulder before darting past Emerson and seeing a low cross deflect into the side netting.
Wolves get their first corner of the game.
Wolves go short from the set-piece, and Ait-Nouri lifts a tempting cross into the area.
There are no red shirts attacking it, but Richarlison bizarrely puts it behind for another corner on the far side.

GOOOOOOOOOAAAAALLLLLLLL! GOMES PUTS WOLVES AHEAD! The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is silenced as Sarabia's inswinging corner finds Gomes around eight yards out, and left totally unmarked, the Brazilian plants his header into the top-left corner.
Wolves have a deserved lead shortly before half-time! 1-0!
Sarabia gets the assist, lifting his set-piece delivery onto the head of Gomes, but where was the Tottenham marking? Gomes was completely alone!
Wolves are still getting so much space to break on Spurs, who look short-handed every time they lose possession.
This time, Hwang almost wriggles away down the left, but Romero recovers to snuff out the danger.
We will have four minutes of stoppage time to end this first half.
GREAT SAVE, but the flag is up anyway! Dawson swings a lovely cross towards the far post, where Sarabia comes in on Davies' blind side to cushion a volley towards goal.
Vicario dives down to his right to push it away, only for Sarabia to be ruled offside – still, Vicario didn't know that!
Wolves are furious as Spurs play on with Lemina down, and Dawson has to scuttle across to prod a left-wing cross behind for a corner.
The set-piece is lifted towards the far post, where Kilman rises to clear.
Wide! Wolves break on Spurs again and Sarabia finds a pocket of space on the right side of the box to take in Ait-Nouri's pass.
He looks for the far corner with an audacious attempt, but there's not enough curl on it!
HALF-TIME: TOTTENHAM 0-1 WOLVES.

It's half-time at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and Wolves are halfway to their first Premier League double over Spurs since 2009-10! O'Neil's team have been excellent from the off, sitting back to frustrate their hosts before striking on the break time and again.

Hwang missed a glaring opportunity to give them an early lead, but Gomes made no mistake when he was left unmarked from Sarabia's 43rd-minute corner, planting his header past a helpless Vicario! In the midst of a tense battle for a top-four finish, Postecoglou's men need to show far more after the break.

Wolves have only had around 35 per cent of the possession so far, but they have managed six shots to Tottenham's five, four attempts on target to none for the hosts, and have generated 0.58 expected goals (xG) to Spurs' 0.37.
The longer this game goes on, the more the likes of Neto, Hwang and Sarabia will look to exploit Tottenham's high line on the break.
We're back under way for the second half, with no changes made by either team.
Wolves get the ball rolling again through Hwang.

GOOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLL! TOTTENHAM LEVEL IMMEDIATELY! Spurs need less than 40 seconds to equalise after the restart! They work the ball into the box through a throw-in on the right-hand side, with Richarlison holding it up for Kulusevski, who tricks his way past Dawson before prodding past Sa from a tight angle.
It's fair to say that goal has changed the mood here! Spurs come again in search of a quickfire second, but Richarlison is caught offside after Maddison's shot deflects through to him off Lemina.
OVER! Tottenham's tails are up now! Kilman concedes a corner, which Maddison swings into the six-yard box.
Richarlison gets there first, but he can't keep his header down!
Tottenham have conceded first in three previous home Premier League games this season, and they have gone on to win all of those matches – against Sheffield United, Brentford and Brighton.
Can they go on to complete the turnaround now?
Wolves just need to enjoy a spell on the ball to take the sting out of this game.
Spurs are well on top, with Emerson stepping infield to win a free-kick off Toti.
This set-piece is around 30 yards out in a central position, and Maddison is over it.
Maddison sprays it wide to Son, who looks to hit the byline and cross, only to send his delivery straight into the gloves of Sa.
Wolves, though, immediately concede possession again through Kilman.
It's all Tottenham at present.
Kulusevski's goal has, of course, extended Tottenham's scoring streak to 37 successive Premier League games.
Twenty-five of those have come under Postecoglou, who has been a breath of fresh air since arriving last year.

WHAT A CHANCE FOR WOLVES! The visitors should be ahead again, but Vicario has bailed his team out! Dawson sprays a wonderful pass out to Semedo on the right-hand side, and he immediately plays it low into the centre for Sarabia.
The Spaniard shoots first-time, but Vicario stands up to smother it and Van de Ven completes the clearance.
Now Tottenham come forward at the other end, but Toti steps across Kulusevski to recover possession inside his own box before the visitors play their way out neatly.
We have a game on our hands here!

Wolves recently went 14 Premier League matches in London without a victory, but they have won their last two in the capital in convincing fashion, beating Brentford 4-1 in December and Chelsea 4-2 earlier this month.
They last won three successive top-flight games in London in September 1979.
STUNNING SAVE FROM SA! Tottenham move the ball beautifully around the edge of the area, with Bissouma and Maddison involved before Kulusevski shoots first-time.
His effort looks destined to find the bottom-right corner, but Sa's outstretched fingertips turn it wide.
Great goalkeeping!
Tottenham fail to make anything of their latest corner, but they regain possession and push Wolves back again.
Son drives infield from the left before finding Richarlison, but Lemina reads the Brazilian's attempted return pass.
ANOTHER CHANCE! Bissouma hares back to prevent a break from Hwang, then sets Tottenham off on another attack.
A left-wing cross deflects out to Kulusevski, who sees his side-footed attempt blocked behind by Semedo.
Wolves are coming under real pressure here!

GOOOOOOOAAAAAAAALLLLLL! GOMES AGAIN FOR WOLVES, WHAT A GOAL! There's the sucker-punch! Tottenham's latest corner is cleared out to Neto, who embarks on a stunning solo run downfield with little support.
Emerson tries to stick with him, but he cuts back onto his left foot before finding Gomes, who arrives in the area to blast past Vicario! What a counterattack, and it's 2-1 to Wolves!
That is one of the assists of the season from Neto.
He charges down the right wing with absolutely no support whatsoever, before checking back and offloading to Gomes, who fires home!
Gomes only had one Premier League goal to his name before this game, hitting the winner in a 2-1 victory at Southampton last February.
He's trebled his tally here, against a team who have been linked with a move for him!
Now Gomes goes into the book for a tactical foul on Emerson, who was threatening to escape over halfway.
Wolves have won two of their last three away Premier League games, as many victories as they managed in their previous 17 (two wins, three draws, 12 defeats).
Are they on course for another successful road trip?
OVER! Semedo slides in but can only clear to a white shirt, and Wolves are under pressure again.
Maddison opens up his body before shooting from the edge of the box, and it just spins over Sa's crossbar – the goalkeeper was worried about that one!
Now Kilman is forced to cut out Sarr's deep cross towards the far post, nodding it behind for a corner.
Maddison delivers to the front post this time, but Gomes heads it clear.
We're about to see changes from both managers, as Maddison's ambitious ball over the top runs away from Davies in the left-hand channel.
Twenty minutes to play.
Postecoglou makes three substitutions in one go.
Werner replaces Bissouma in an attacking change.
Johnson, who hit the winner against Brighton last week, is on for Richarlison.
The third change comes in midfield, with Bentancur on for Sarr.
And here comes O'Neil's first alteration.
Sarabia is withdrawn, having laid on Wolves' first goal.
Bellegarde will offer fresh legs and pace on the break as he comes on.
Tottenham forward Johnson has scored on two of his last three Premier League appearances, with both goals coming off the bench (against Brighton and Brentford).
The only previous Spurs player to score from three successive substitute appearances in the competition was Teddy Sheringham in 1994.
The home fans aren't happy as Semedo wins a foul against Kulusevski, stopping another Tottenham attack in its tracks and slowing the pace of the game.
The travelling Wolves supporters are in fine voice behind Sa's goal.
Now Hwang backs into Van de Ven to win what looked like a cheap free-kick inside the Tottenham half.
Neto will swing this one into the penalty area... and he finds Ait-Nouri unmarked at the far post, but his touch just runs away from him! That was a good opportunity!
Spurs have a very attack-minded XI out there now, with Werner playing centrally and Kulusevski, Son and Maddison in support.
Wolves are continuing to defend deep and wait for an opportunity to break.
Emerson gets the ball out of his feet and drives a low cross into the six-yard box, where Dawson sends an awkward clearance spinning behind for a corner.
The set-piece is lifted into the danger zone, but Dawson gets up again to clear!
MASSIVE CHANCE FOR 3-1! Bellegarde should put the game to bed! Hwang breaks from the Tottenham corner, finding Neto in space out on the right.
He plays a well weighted pass between two Spurs defenders to pick out Bellegarde, but the substitute tries to do too much! He sits Bentancur down before seeing his shot blocked by Emerson!
Great defending from Toti as we enter the last 10 minutes of the 90, sliding in on Kulusevski to win the ball and play it behind off the winger, winning a goal-kick!
Half a chance! Bellegarde darts forward to win a corner on the Wolves right, which is delivered deep towards Lemina.
Dawson keeps his header alive and helps it back out to Lemina, who sees his snapshot held by Vicario.
Wolves continue to carry a threat.
Wolves have everyone back around their own area as Spurs work it patiently from side from side.
Werner stands up a cross, but Toti nods it out before Gomes completes the clearance.
Eight to play.
SAVE! The ball is worked right by Bentancur, and Emerson finds space to shoot.
His effort skids off the surface and is held well by Sa, with multiple Tottenham players closing in for a rebound!
Postecoglou is preparing two further changes to his midfield, with Lo Celso and Hojbjerg ready to enter the fray.
Son faces up to Semedo on the Tottenham left, and his low cross is put behind for another corner.

Great defending! Spurs' corner is cleared but Neto hesitates and allows the hosts to recover possession, only for Semedo to get his body between Werner and the ball to shepherd it out for a goal-kick – good play!
Here come the Spurs changes.
Hojbjerg is on for Maddison.
Lo Celso, meanwhile, replaces Emerson in another positive switch.
Wolves aren't happy as Tottenham play on despite Hwang being down with a head injury, but Kilman puts his foot through a clearance and the visitors will make a change of their own now.
Traore replaces Hwang as O'Neil adds bodies to his midfield, with two minutes plus stoppage time to play.
Over! Bellegarde latches onto a loose Tottenham pass and advances to the halfway line before threading a pass through for Neto on his left.
The winger gets to the edge of the box before shooting, but he sends a tired effort spinning into the stands behind the goal.
Half a chance! Ait-Nouri fouls Johnson to grant Tottenham a free-kick on the right wing.
Kulusevski's deep cross finds Van de Ven... but his glancing header is straight at Sa!
We will have FIVE minutes of stoppage time here! Can Wolves hold on?
Bellegarde tricks his way to the byline before standing up a cross for Neto, who sends a wild volley high and wide.
That will be the winger's final involvement, as Doherty replaces him.
DANGER! Werner plays a give-and-go with Son and tries to find space for a shot in a crowded penalty area.
His strike hits Dawson and finds its way back to Sa, and the home fans scream for handball, but it's more in hope than expectation.
Nothing doing!
HUGE CHANCE! Kulusevski teases a brilliant cross into the six-yard box, where Davies makes a run across his marker to meet it.
He simply has to level the game, but he sends an awkward header spinning comfortably wide of the right-hand post.
What a let-off that is!
FULL-TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-2 WOLVES.

The full-time whistle sounds, and Wolves hold on for a massive win over top-four chasing Tottenham! Gomes is the hero for O'Neil's men, netting either side of half-time in yet another upset of one of the Premier League's elite clubs! Gomes was left totally unmarked for his first goal, a close-range header shortly before half-time, but Tottenham looked the more likely winners when Kulusevski levelled immediately after the restart.
However, Wolves continued to threaten on the break, and Gomes got his second when he crashed home following a brilliant run and pass from the electric Neto.
Tottenham dominated possession from there, but Davies missed their best chance in stoppage time as the likes of Semedo and Toti produced colossal defensive performances.
The win takes Wolves up to 35 points, two points off the top seven, while Tottenham slip to fifth following Aston Villa's 2-1 win at Fulham.
That's all from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, so thank you for your company and goodbye!
